title: Austin: Amusements Censorship & Vagrancy Fine
summary:
*   A delegation formally requested the city consider censorship of public amusements.
*   The Auditorium Fund was discontinued, with its remaining balance transferred to other purposes.
*   An ordinance revising the duties of the Fire Marshal was approved.
*   A vagrancy fine for a young man was remitted due to his youth and mitigating circumstances.

APPROVED, Dec. 19, 1918: A. P. Wooldridge, Mayor. Fire marshal
Ordinance
Amended
The Mayor laid before the Council "An ordinance amending Section six of an ordinance
entitled 'An ordinance creating the office of Fire Marshal, prescribing the duties thereof
and prescribing penalties for violations,' passed by the City Council of the City of
Austin, Texas, June 9th, 1910." The ordinance was read the first time, after which the
Mayor moved a suspension of the rule and the placing of the ordinance upon its second
reading. The motion prevailed by a vote of 5 yeas, no nays.
After the ordinance had been read the second time, the Mayor moved a further suspension of
the rule and the placing of it on its third reading. This motion carried by a vote of 5
yeas, no nays.
When the ordinance had been read the third time, the Mayor moved its final passage, the
motion prevailing by the following vote: Yeas, Mayor Wooldridge, Councilman Anthony,
Bartholomew, Haynes, and Powell, 5; nays none.
The Council then adjourned.

E. Martin
City Clerk

SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL: Austin, Texas, Dec. 20, 1918.

The Council met with all members present.
Councilman Anthony offered the following resolution: C. B. Coffield
Fine
RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AUSTIN: That the unpaid balance of the fine
and costs ($50.00 fine and $14.80 costs) assessed against C. B. Coffield for vagrancy in
Cause No. 13156, Corporation Court of this city, said balance amounting to $50.80, be and
the same is hereby remitted. This action is taken, upon the recommendation of the
Assistant City Attorney, because of the youth of the said Coffield and the existence of
mitigating circumstances in his case. Also, it is believed that, having worked out $14.00
of the said fine and costs, the young man has been sufficiently punished.
The resolution was adopted by a vote of 5 yeas, no nays.
APPROVED, Dec. 20, 1918: A. P. Wooldridge, Mayor.

E. Martin
City Clerk
